scenario.title: Social Circles
scenario.premise: Partners coordinate introductions into each other's social circles.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: My friends are having dinner Sunday, and I would like you to come with me.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I would be glad to meet them. Is there anything I should know?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: They are warm, and I will stay close if you need a break.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Thank you. I want to know the people important to you.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I am excited to bring my partner into the social circle that matters to me.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I understand. Did you sleep well after we turned the lights out early?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I did, and waking up without rushing made the morning gentler.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Would you like to keep the same bedtime tonight?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, if we finish the kitchen cleanup before we get tired.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I can wash the dishes if you clear the counter.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: That split works, and I will put the leftovers away too.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Could you label the container for tomorrow?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Of course, and I will leave it on the front shelf where we can see it.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Thank you. Do we need anything else for breakfast?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: We have enough fruit, but we are nearly out of oats.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I can add oats to our shared list.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Please do, and I will check whether we need more tea.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: The tea is still fine. How is your energy for work today?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Better than yesterday, though I need a quiet hour before my first call.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Would it help if I used the other room during that hour?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, thank you. I will let you know as soon as the call ends.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Do you want encouragement before it starts or space to focus?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: A quick good-luck message would feel nice, then space until I finish.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I can do that. What is the hardest part of the call?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Explaining the delay clearly without sounding defensive.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Could you lead with what changed and what you can do next?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: That would keep it practical. I will write those two points down.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Would you like me to listen to the opening once?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, after lunch, when I have shaped it into a complete thought.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: That timing works for me. I have a deadline before lunch too.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I will keep the common room quiet so we can both concentrate.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I appreciate that. Shall we take a short break together at noon?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, ten minutes by the window would help both of us reset.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Would you rather have soup or sandwiches for lunch?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Soup sounds better, and I can warm it while you finish your note.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Could we add the bread left from yesterday?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, I will toast it so it does not go to waste.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I like how we have been using what we already have.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Me too. It saves money and makes the kitchen easier to manage.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Should we review the food budget this evening?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: That would be useful, as long as we keep it to twenty minutes.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Twenty minutes is enough. What should we look at first?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: The recent grocery totals, then one change we both can maintain.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I would rather adjust snacks than cut the meals we enjoy.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I agree. A plan has to support us, not make every meal stressful.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Could we each choose one favourite snack for the week?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, that feels fair and still keeps the list simple.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Could we also open the calendar and check the weekend?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, I see the family lunch and the repair appointment.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Do you still have energy for the family lunch?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I do, but I would like us to leave before the evening gets too full.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: What departure time would feel comfortable?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Around four, with a little flexibility if the conversation is winding down.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I can support that. Would you like me to mention our timing early?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Please, so leaving does not feel sudden or personal.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I will say we already have a quiet evening planned.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Thank you. That is true and gives us a clear boundary.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Before we wrap up, can we return to what we said earlier?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, I have one more thought about it.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I feel secure in the relationship we have built as partners, including in ordinary moments.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I am excited too.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: We will go together.
